summary: THE FORK RESOLVES ON A THIRD HORN, and it is the honest one: ep 53 adapts NOTHING between ch 110 and ch 109 in the anime's own order, and ep 54's stored START 109 is NOT the error either — ep 53 is an anime-original episode wedged into the 110/109 reorder, so the crossing is a hole only in the sense that ep 53 takes no anchor (A1). Delivered as anchor_hostile for ep 53 + a type correction canon -> FILLER, while the one anchor in this verdict is ep 52's confirmation (END 110 [110]), and ep 52's END 110 and ep 54's START 109 are both re-confirmed ON THE PAGES. THE PAGES (all three chapters read image by image from MangaDex, printed tankobon numbering, v13 = 107-115, the space the stored volume table and every source here use): ch 110 'Regime of Terror' (22 images: body pp.2-21, p.22 an Investigation-Corner omake) is the whole Zokugaku-vs-Kyoshin match and its last body page is the double spread of Habashira crying 'JUST WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN US?! YOU AND ME!' — which is verbatim the closing beat en-WP and Plex give for EP 52 ('In the end, Rui confronts Hiruma and cries out through his tears, "What exactly is the difference between you and me?!"'), so ep 52 = ch 110 start to finish, END 110 [110] CONFIRMED. ch 109 'Sting' (20 images: p.1 a scanlation credit page, p.2 the chapter opening, p.3 the title page, pp.4-19 the body, p.20 an omake) is the ENTIRE Deimon-vs-Dokubari game in ONE chapter: it opens on 9/25 at the stadium with Deimon already wearing rouge (Hiruma: 'I meant that you should BRING rouge to today's match, NOT to put it on!'), introduces the Scorpions' 10-wins-1-loss record and Kanagushi's 'American football is a mind game that's fought using your head', runs his habit-reading (the QB licking his fingers, the linemen's weight tilt, where the receiver looks first), is countered by the rouge turning EVERY Deimon fingertip red, and ends 'DEIMON'S COMPLETE VICTORY!! DOKUBARI SCORPIONS 0 - 42 DEIMON DEVILBATS ... Finally at the quarter-finals...!! Now there're 8 teams left.' HIRUMA IS PRESENT ON THE FIELD FOR THE WHOLE CHAPTER ('There's nobody who can beat Hiruma'), and ch 108's last body page (checked) is the all-you-can-eat barbecue — the manga has NO pre-game Scorpions material anywhere. WHAT EP 53 ACTUALLY IS: the licensor's own synopsis (TV Tokyo back-number episodes05, live; the same text on Bandai Channel 8777/053) says the Scorpions are a team that 'has driven its opponents into suspension or forfeit by underhanded means', Kanagushi declares war and springs 'dangerous traps' on Sena and co whose REAL target is Hiruma, and on game day Hiruma never appears — kickoff arrives with the team rattled. A per-episode watch-along beat list (itsahanzo, 2009) fills it in: tacks in Sena's shoes, a shot put out of nowhere, loosened bolts at a construction site, Hiruma kidnapped in the night, Kurita made captain, ISHIMARU appointed QB, and the Scorpions taking a 14-0 LEAD. Not one of those events exists in ch 108-111; the manga's game is a 0-42 shutout with Hiruma running it. The fandom's own Dokubari Scorpions page states the score twice — '0-42 (Manga), 14-42 (Anime)' — and its Kanagushi page attributes the abduction explicitly to the anime ('In the anime Kanagushi also became Hiruma's slave, by accidentally saying his plan to capture Hiruma and keeping him away from the game aloud'). CH 109 IS EP 54's, PAGE FOR PAGE: the blog's ep-54 beats are 'He later asked the team to put on lipsticks and even on their finger tips. Dokubari Scorpions is reading their finger tips on their game play through the rush of blood ... Hiruma completely read the opponents play and won the match 42-14', i.e. ch 109 pp.2, 8-10 and the closing spread; en-WP's ep-54 line agrees ('Mamori opens the game plan Hiruma gave her ... At last Hiruma appears. The Devil Bats win the game'); and the fandom's ch-109 page carries the reverse mapping `episode = [[Episode 54]]` and nothing else. So the stored ep 54 START 109 is CORRECT and no repair is owed on it — the second horn of the fork is refuted, not merely unproven. WHAT REMAINS OF THE SOURCE IN EP 53 IS A SLIVER: the Scorpions' introduction — the 10-wins-1-loss record (ch 109 p.5, Kumabukuro's line) and Kanagushi's 'football is a mind game' premise (ch 109 p.6, the beat Plex/TVDB's ep-53 blurb names) — transplanted out of the stadium into the anime's pre-game build-up and re-glossed ('half of it was won through forfeits'). weight: SLIVER — a two-panel stat and a one-line premise lifted out of a chapter that ep 54 adapts properly and in full; it earns no type, and ep 53 takes no anchor (A1) under the T28 sliver clause — the only anchor delivered here is ep 52's confirmation. The episode's job is the sabotage-and-abduction plot and an invented first quarter, so the remainder decides: FILLER. THE ONE DISSENT, stated plainly: ja-WP's 各話リスト leaves ep 53's 備考 EMPTY while marking ep 51 right above it アニメオリジナルストーリー — a real control, not silence. I read it as ja-WP marking only WHOLLY original stories: ep 53 is the first half of a match the manga does contain, so a Japanese editor would not call the episode オリジナル even though every event in it is invented. Against that stand the pages themselves, the fandom's Category:Anime-Original Episodes (whose 34 members are otherwise a superset of our own filler set — it also holds 74/88/126/128, all rows we type mixed), and AFG's '* Filler'. Two source-side caveats declared: (1) TV Tokyo and Bandai Channel print the SAME synopsis text for eps 53/54 — one licensor lineage, not two (b-ch is independent only for eps 51/52, which TV Tokyo's archive starts too late to hold); (2) every eyeshield21.fandom episode and chapter page in this zone was created or rewritten by ONE editor, Whiteknight810210, on 2026-06-24 / 07-09 / 07-18 — a single lineage, cited as such. AFL has no page for this series at all (404, matching the context's 'AFL: —'), and AFG's Chapters column is empty for every row from the 40s on (the documented mid-series stop; an empty cell is not 'no chapter').

anchor_hostile.why: A1 + T28 (the sliver clause): a filler row takes no anchor, and there is no position to give it even if it did. The episode's plot — Kanagushi declaring war, tacks in Sena's shoes, a shot put thrown at him, loosened bolts at a construction site, Hiruma abducted the night before, Kurita made captain, Ishimaru at quarterback, the Scorpions leading 14-0 — has no counterpart anywhere in the manga: ch 108 ends on the all-you-can-eat barbecue, ch 109 opens on the morning of the match with Hiruma already on the field and closes 0-42 in Deimon's favour, and ch 110/111 are the Zokugaku-Kyoshin match and the quarter-final bracket. The only source material in the row is the Scorpions' INTRODUCTION lifted out of ch 109's stadium scene — their 10-wins-1-loss record (ch 109 p.5) and Kanagushi's 'American football is a mind game' premise (ch 109 p.6) — relocated into the anime's pre-game build-up and re-glossed ('half of it was won through forfeits'). weight: SLIVER — a stat panel and a one-line premise, carried here as framing for an invented plot, while ch 109 itself is adapted properly and in full by ep 54 (the rouge, the red fingertips, Hiruma out-reading Kanagushi, the 42-point rout). Under the sliver clause that segment earns neither a type nor an anchor; it is noted as `graft{109}` and the remainder of the episode decides the standing. An END of 109 here would be false in both directions: it would claim pages ep 54 owns, and it would tell a reader that ch 109 had been animated when what they watched was invented. A44 also applies in its own right — the material is another episode's chapter, restaged out of position. THE ONE COUNTER-READING, on the record: ja-WP's 各話リスト leaves ep 53's 備考 empty while marking ep 51 directly above it アニメオリジナルストーリー; on my reading ja-WP marks only wholly-original STORIES and ep 53 is half of a match the manga does contain, but it is a genuine dissent and not silence.

annotations.note: The episode's plot is the anime's own and contradicts the source's account of the same match. Manga (ch 109, read page by page): Hiruma is on the field from the first snap, has already had the team bring rouge, turns Kanagushi's habit-reading against him, and Deimon shuts the Scorpions out 0-42 inside a single chapter. Anime (eps 53-54): Kanagushi runs a sabotage campaign against Sena (tacks, a shot put, loosened bolts) whose real target is Hiruma, Hiruma is abducted the night before the match, Kurita takes the captaincy and Ishimaru plays quarterback, the Scorpions lead 14-0, and Hiruma only returns in the second quarter (ep 54) — final score 42-14. The fandom records both scores side by side ('0-42 (Manga), 14-42 (Anime)') and attributes the abduction plot to the anime on Kanagushi's own page. This is an original share, not a faithfulness alteration: the events are added, not cut, reordered or condensed.

flags_for_sean: OUT OF ASK, an enrichment I could not close: ep 54's stored END 111 may be a TITLE-shaped pin. Chapter 111 '8強の世界' / 'World of the Quarter-Finals' (20 pages, read) is (a) the Ojo-vs-Sengoku third-round game with the Sengoku coach and the chained Ikari teased, (b) a full double-spread of the quarter-final bracket — 'Spiders vs Fighters / Fishers vs Gunmans / Pirates vs Whiteknights / Poseidon vs Devilbats', (c) Kyoshin's QB Kobanzame spying on Deimon, (d) Deimon practising on stilts to simulate Kyoshin's height, and (e) Sena/Monta/Komusubi going to Kyoshin High. NONE of (a) or (c)-(e) appears in either beat list for ep 54, whose last beat is 'Deimon Devil Bats advance as the best of 8 teams' — which is also ch 109's own closing line ('Finally at the quarter-finals...!! Now there're 8 teams left'). The defensible reading is that ep 54 carries ch 111 only as the BRACKET SPLASH (pp.5-6), i.e. a partial, which is enough to keep the END at 111 under A4 but wants a `partial{111}` annotation rather than a bare range; the alternative reading is that the 111 pin came from the chapter's TITLE matching the episode's ending, which is the documented eyeshield trap (ep 32 borrows ch 86's title while adapting ch 79). I did not propose a repair: settling it needs eps 55 and 57 read as well (ep 57 「21」を知る者 is where the anime puts the Kyoshin-practice spying that ch 111 (e) sets up), and those rows are outside this ask.

OUT OF ASK, an observation on ep 53's opening: the watch-along records the episode opening with Seibu, Ojo, Bando and Kyoshin all reaching the best 8. In the manga those results are stated across ch 109's last page and ch 111's bracket.
